My take on each rule.

I am in favor of removing rule 5. I've had some issues with it as people can't, technically, post youtube videos/etc, which is where a lot of news content is coming from these days.

Rule 0: I do want to get rid of this one. If others are fine with if, I want to allow for people to post discussion-type submissions.

Rule 1: Keep this. This rule is just highlighting good practice.

Rule 2: I don't think this is a bad rule. It keeps people from posting articles/whatever that is old. Many times, things are posted that are form years ago that may seem like that are relevant today (for example, when people post videos of voter fraud from an election cycle ago). /v/worldnews is supposed to be about current world happenings, not have may have happened X months ago.

Rule 3: Two sides to this. The side that wants to remove this is rather obvious, it can allow the moderators to more arbitrarily remove posts that they may not like. On the other hand, it helps to stop people from posting articles that are perversions of the truth, just to get traction. If the original article is editorialized and the user editorializes it to reflect the truth, then that post shouldn't be removed. It's only when an editorialization leads to misinformation that it should be removed. . The reason this rule exists is to help stop misinformation from spreading around. We could go the route of /v/videos where they have a "nebulous title" flair, but no one outside of the sub actually sees that flair, so anyone seeing it on the front page doesn't realize from face value that the title may be misleading.

Rule 4: I see no problem with this rule. I believe moderators should be able to delete posts that are clearly ads, spam, or just ways for people to try and earn money form users (ref-links). Of course, I'm all up for a discussion on this one.

Rule 5: I'm definitely fine with getting rid of this one. I was considering bringing it up myself, but hadn't decided on doing it yet.

Rule 6: I'm fine with revising this one to "No overuse of Caps-lock." The whole "use correct capitalization" is kind of ambiguous; who decides what is "correct capitalization?"

Rule 7&8: There's no harm in this one, in my opinion. Though I believe we should revise this to allow for people to post translations as the original link.
